Individual metabolic laboratory abnormalities also warrant further assessment in future prospective trials.

items.title: Visual feedback increases expiratory muscle training effort in Parkinson's disease: a randomised crossover trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disorders of airway protection, including impaired cough and swallowing, are clinically important complications of Parkinson's disease. Expiratory muscle strength training (EMST) is an established non-pharmacological intervention targeting these deficits. The aim of this study was to evaluate the acute effect of visual feedback provided by the SpiroGym mHealth app on expiratory muscle activation during EMST in people with Parkinson's disease.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, randomised, two-period crossover trial in people with Parkinson's disease. Participants performed EMST under two conditions, in randomised order: conventional EMST without visual feedback and EMST with real-time visual feedback provided by the SpiroGym app. Expiratory muscle activation was measured using surface electromyography of the abdominal muscles. The primary outcome was the within-participant difference in mean peak normalised internal oblique activity between conditions. Secondary outcomes included external oblique and rectus abdominis activity, associations with neuropsychiatric symptoms, and participant-reported usability ratings.
RESULTS: Twenty participants were randomised, and 19 completed the study and were included in the final analysis. No study-related adverse events occurred. Visual feedback significantly increased mean peak normalised internal oblique activity compared with no feedback (118.2 ± 36.4% vs. 90.5 ± 23.0% of reference voluntary contraction; p < 0.001; Cohen d = 0.95). Without feedback, internal oblique activation significantly declined from 100.1 ± 22.2% in the first set to 84.4 ± 25.5% in the fifth set, whereas it remained stable with feedback (120.3 ± 29.4% to 119.9 ± 40.6%). External oblique activation was also significantly higher with feedback (122.2 ± 38.1% vs. 100.9 ± 32.4%; p = 0.002; Cohen d = 0.66), while rectus abdominis activation did not differ significantly between conditions (105.2 ± 41.3% vs. 90.2 ± 36.1%; p = 0.06; Cohen d = 0.43). No significant associations between feedback responsiveness and depression, apathy, or anxiety were detected. Participants rated the visual feedback as easy to understand and helpful for EMST performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Real-time visual feedback delivered by the SpiroGym app acutely increased and stabilized expiratory muscle activation during EMST in people with Parkinson's disease. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06942533, 1 May 2025.

items.title: AI-Enabled Telerehabilitation for Chronic Nonspecific Neck Pain: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise therapy is effective in managing chronic nonspecific neck pain (CNP). Nevertheless, the high burden of CNP continues to place pressure on existing rehabilitation services, especially in remote or resource-constrained settings where continuous and standardized physical therapy may be difficult to access. By combining home-based exercise with remote supervision and movement feedback, AI-enabled telerehabilitation may broaden access to rehabilitation and support the continued management of CNP.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether an AI-enabled telerehabilitation program was noninferior to standard outpatient rehabilitation for improving neck-related disability in individuals with CNP and compared the effects of the 2 interventions on pain, health-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, parallel-group randomized noninferiority trial was conducted at Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Beijing Jishuitan Hospital. Patients with CNP of at least 3 months' duration were randomized 1:1 to a telerehabilitation group (TG) or outpatient rehabilitation group (OG) using concealed, web-based, variable blocks stratified by center and baseline Neck Disability Index (NDI) severity. Both groups completed identical 24-week strengthening and stretching programs (3 sessions per wk; ≈30 min per session) and were assessed at weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, and 24. TG trained at home using sensor-based movement recognition and threshold rules; OG received face-to-face outpatient rehabilitation. Week-24 NDI was the primary outcome; Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), EQ-5D, and cervical range of motion were secondary. Noninferiority required the upper 95% CI bound of the TG-OG NDI difference to be <10 percentage points (5/50). Analyses were intention-to-treat; assessors and statisticians were blinded.
RESULTS: Of 312 individuals screened, 116 were randomized (58 per group). At week 24, 55 TG and 53 OG participants completed assessments; all 116 participants were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis using observed or imputed data. The between-group differences in NDI (TG - OG) were -2.8 (95% CI -6.3 to 0.7; P=.11) at week 12 and -2.5 (95% CI -6.2 to 1.2; P=.15) at week 24. At week 24, the upper 95% CI bound was below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 10 percentage points on the 0 to 100 NDI scale, equivalent to 5 points on the original 0 to 50 scale, demonstrating noninferiority of TG. Both groups showed clinically meaningful reductions in NDI, with comparable improvements in NPRS, EQ-5D, and cervical range of motion. No intervention-related harms occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Over 24 weeks, AI-enabled telerehabilitation was noninferior to exercise-matched outpatient rehabilitation for neck-related disability, with broadly comparable improvements in pain, health-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion. AI-enabled telerehabilitation may be a practical alternative for patients with CNP who are unable to attend outpatient rehabilitation.

items.title: Clinical outcomes of low versus high intensity laser therapy in patients with subacute carpal tunnel syndrome: A randomized, single-blinded, controlled trial.
items.abstract: A common entrapment of median nerve that causes pain, numbness, and functional impairment is called Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS). Laser therapy is a noninvasive intervention for neural repair and pain modulation, but comparative evidence between Low-Level Laser Therapy (LLLT) and High-Intensity Laser Therapy (HILT) in subacute CTS is limited. The aims of this study were to compare the effects of LLLT and HILT on pain, functional status, electrophysiological, and ultrasonographic parameters in subacute CTS. A single-blinded randomized controlled trial (Reg. No. IRCT20241111063665N1) was conducted at the Department of Physiotherapy, The University of Lahore (UOL), Lahore, Pakistan, from August 2024 to March 2025. Sixty-nine participants with subacute CTS, confirmed by electromyography and nerve conduction studies, were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 23 each): Group A (HILT; 808 nm + physiotherapy), Group B (LLLT; 860 nm + physiotherapy), and Group C (physiotherapy + sham laser). Assessments were at baseline and week 6. Outcomes included pain (VAS), symptom severity and functional status (Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire; BCTQ), grip strength, distal motor latency (DML), sensory nerve conduction velocity (SNCV), and median nerve cross-sectional area (CSA). ANCOVA with Bonferroni correction and effect size estimation was applied. At week 6, both HILT and LLLT showed significant improvements (p < 0.001). HILT achieved greater pain reduction (- 4.9) than LLLT (- 4.1) and control (- 2.2; p < 0.001), with greater improvement in BCTQ-SSS (- 2.2 points), BCTQ-FSS (- 1.9 points), grip strength (+ 9.9 kg), DML (- 1.2 ms), SNCV (+ 12.3 m/s), and CSA (- 3.7 mm²). Large effect sizes (Cohen's d > 0.8) were observed. Both LLLT and HILT are effective as adjuncts to physiotherapy in subacute CTS. HILT demonstrated greater improvements than LLLT within the parameters tested.Clinical Trial Number: IRCT20241111063665N1, Registration date: 17 March, 2025.

items.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of a 6-month supervised multicomponent telerehabilitation programme combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release on fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, and psychological outcomes.
DESIGN: Two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial.
SUBJECTS/PATIENTS: 68 adults with fibromyalgia confirmed according to the 2016 ACR criteria.
METHODS: Participants were randomized to a 6-month supervised home-based telerehabilitation programme (n = 35) or usual care (n = 33). The intervention comprised 3 live online sessions weekly combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise, self-myofascial release, core stabilization, low-load resistance exercise, stretching, and relaxation. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months using validated patient-reported measures.
RESULTS: Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for fibromyalgia impact (p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.132), sleep quality (p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.129), depressive symptoms (p = 0.002, partial η2 = 0.129), and perceived stress (p = 0.028, partial η2 = 0.065), but not for anxiety (p = 0.701). Mean intervention adherence was 87.5%, with no adverse or serious adverse events reported in either group.
CONCLUSION: 6 months of supervised multicomponent telerehabilitation produced favourable longitudinal changes in fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and perceived stress compared with usual care.

items.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
items.abstract:
QUESTION: In adults with chronic non-specific low back pain, does adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to a program of motor control exercise (MCE) improve pain intensity, disability and circulating prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) concentrations compared with sham PBMT plus MCE?
DESIGN: A randomised controlled trial was conducted with concealed allocation, intention-to-treat analysis and blinding of participants, therapists and assessors.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged 18 to 65 years seeking treatment for chronic non-specific low back pain of ≥ 3 months in duration.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly allocated to active PBMT plus MCE or sham PBMT plus MCE. Both groups received 12 treatment sessions over 6 weeks.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Assessments were completed at baseline and 6 weeks, with follow-up assessments at 1 month after the end of the intervention period and at 3, 6 and 12 months after randomisation. Primary outcomes were pain intensity (0 to 10 numerical rating scale) and disability (0 to 24 Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire) at 6 weeks, in which higher scores indicated greater severity. Secondary outcomes were: pain and disability at follow-up timepoints; circulating PGE2 concentrations at 6 weeks; and medication use, concomitant care and adverse events throughout the follow-up period.
RESULTS: A total of 148 participants were randomised (74 per group). The intention-to-treat analysis showed that PBMT plus MCE had a negligible effect compared with sham plus MCE at 6 weeks for pain intensity (MD -0.4 points, 95% CI -1.2 to 0.4), disability (MD -0.7 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 0.9) or circulating PGE2 concentrations (MD 31 pg/ml, 95% CI -4 to 66). Negligible between-group differences were observed throughout the 12-month follow-up period, and no treatment-related adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: Adding PBMT to MCE did not provide clinically important additional improvements in pain intensity, disability or circulating PGE2 concentrations compared with sham plus the same exercise program.
REGISTRATION: NCT05487118.

items.title: Feasibility of a brief sequential sleep and physical activity behavioral intervention in African American adults with overweight or obesity.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short sleep duration and low physical activity commonly co-occur among African American (AA) adults with overweight or obesity and are associated with adverse health outcomes, including type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, stroke, and premature mortality. However, limited evidence addresses whether the sequence of sleep and physical activity intervention components is feasible or associated with short-term behavioral outcomes.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of delivering sequential sleep and physical activity interventions in alternate order and to descriptively characterize changes in sleep, sedentary behavior, and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in a randomized pilot sequencing trial.
METHODS: Thirty AA adults with body mass index ≥25 kg m², short sleep duration, and low physical activity were randomized to Sleep → Physical Activity, Physical Activity → Sleep, or a contact-matched control condition. Each active intervention sequence included two 4-week phases separated by a 1-week interval. Assessments at baseline, week 5, and week 9 included 7-day wrist actigraphy, daily sleep diary, online questionnaires, and anthropometrics. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, adherence, and participant satisfaction. Baseline-adjusted ANCOVA models examined exploratory week 9 outcomes.
RESULTS: Recruitment (75%) approached the prespecified benchmark (80%), retention met the ≥70% benchmark (70% for Sleep → Physical Activity; 100% for Physical Activity → Sleep; 90% for Control), and mean adherence met the ≥66% criterion (66.7% and 91.7%, respectively). No adverse events occurred. Among respondents with available week 9 satisfaction data, ratings of study procedures, materials, and study service were favorable. In exploratory baseline-adjusted models, no condition effects were observed for actigraphy-measured sleep, sedentary time, MVPA, or Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index global score. Insomnia Severity Index scores at week 9 were lower in Sleep → Physical Activity compared with Physical Activity → Sleep; this finding was exploratory and not adjusted for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Sequential delivery of sleep and physical activity intervention components was feasible in AA adults with overweight or obesity, short sleep duration, and low physical activity. Behavioral outcome findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. Larger trials are needed to evaluate sequencing effects on insomnia symptoms, objective sleep, sedentary behavior, and physical activity.
items.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine

items.title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
items.abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.
items.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

items.title: Recommendations for the development, implementation, and evaluation of technology-assisted physical activity interventions to support healthy aging: insights from PhysAgeNet.
items.abstract: Digital health technologies offer substantial potential to support physical activity among older adults, yet their development and implementation often remain driven by technological possibilities rather than clinical evidence and user needs. This position paper, developed within the PhysAgeNet COST Action, synthesizes current evidence and expert consensus to provide recommendations for designing, evaluating, and implementing technology-assisted physical activity interventions for older adults. We first outline key technology categories and functions relevant to physical activity promotion, including wearables, exergames, mobile applications, telehealth platforms, and smart environments, and highlight critical technical requirements such as accuracy, reliability, connectivity, interoperability, and data security. We then emphasize the need to align digital interventions with established clinical guidelines for physical activity, falls prevention, frailty, and sarcopenia, including explicit specification of exercise dose according to FITT-VP principles and robust monitoring of dual adherence to both physical activity and technology use. Building on technology acceptance models and behavior change theories, we describe how user-centered and co-creative design processes can translate theoretical constructs into concrete digital features that enhance motivation, enjoyment, and long-term engagement. Finally, we propose stakeholder-specific guidance for developers, researchers, and clinicians, including recommendations on user assessment, recruitment of vulnerable groups, implementation frameworks, and clinically grounded evaluation of outcomes and usability. Together, these recommendations provide a pragmatic roadmap for moving from a technology-push paradigm toward evidence-based, acceptable, and equitable technology-assisted physical activity interventions that can be sustainably integrated into routine practice for older adults.

items.title: Supportive Care in Multiple Myeloma: Evidence-Based Recommendations From the Intergroupe Francophone du Myélome (IFM).
items.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a largely incurable plasma cell malignancy in which disease- and treatment-related complications substantially impair quality of life and survival, making supportive care a central determinant of outcome. This review presents unified, evidence-based recommendations from the Intergroupe Francophone du Myélome across 7 domains of supportive care and their implications for contemporary practice, including the era of T-cell-redirecting immunotherapy. With the advent of highly effective induction regimens, autologous stem cell transplantation, immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors, anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs), and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies, the prevention and management of treatment-emergent toxicities and disease-related sequelae have become increasingly complex. Synthesizing a structured review of the literature, international guidelines, and formal expert consensus, we provide practical recommendations for (1) venous thromboembolism prophylaxis, (2) prevention of skeletal-related events with bone-modifying agents, (3) prevention of infectious complications, (4) vaccination, (5) management of MM-related anemia with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, (6) adapted physical activity, and (7) practical guidance for the management of treatment-emergent peripheral neuropathy, with particular attention to the specific challenges introduced by BsAbs and CAR-T therapy. By consolidating these 7 domains into a single framework applicable across all lines of therapy, from first-line treatment to relapsed/refractory disease, this review offers a pragmatic reference intended to standardize and improve supportive care and, ultimately, patient outcomes and health-related quality of life in MM. Positions that deliberately differ from other international guidelines-notably those of the International Myeloma Working Group-are explicitly identified and justified.
items.authors: IFM Supportive Care Working Group i in.

items.title: State of the Evidence and Strength of Recommendations for Interventions Used by Physical Therapists in Children and Adolescents with Autism: An Overview of Systematic Reviews.
items.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the evidence and strength of recommendations for interventions used by physical therapists for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
METHOD: An overview of systematic reviews was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews of Healthcare Interventions statement. Systematic reviews evaluating interventions used by physical therapists for this population were included. Outcomes were categorized according to the ICF framework. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias in Systematic Reviews tool. Quality of evidence and strength of recommendations were evaluated using GRADE and translated into a traffic-light system (green, yellow, or red). A patient and public involvement group, including parents and individuals with ASD, contributed to recommendation evaluation.
RESULTS: Nine reviews, including 53 studies and 1016 participants, identified 11 interventions used by physical therapists. Most studies reported positive effects, mainly on body functions and activities, although evidence quality ranged from very low to low. Most interventions received conditional "yellow light" recommendations, whereas task-specific motor training for gross motor function received a strong "green light" recommendation.
CONCLUSION: Interventions used by physical therapists may benefit children and adolescents with ASD, but evidence remains overall limited and is of low or very low quality.
items.authors: Rodrigues de Sousa Junior R i in.

items.title: Altitude and child development: A cross-sectional comparative study of children in urbanized low-altitude and rural high-altitude settings in Kyrgyzstan.
items.abstract: Childhood malnutrition remains a global challenge; Kyrgyzstan has reduced it, though disparities persist. We hypothesized that developmental differences between lowland and highland children reflect altitude adaptation, not malnutrition alone, obscuring monitoring. This study compared children from Naryn (2400 m) to Bishkek (800 m), examining respiratory, hematological, and anthropometric development. We conducted a cross-sectional study among healthy Kyrgyz schoolchildren aged 10-12 from Naryn and Bishkek. Measurements included anthropometrics, spirometry, hemoglobin, hand-grip strength, and vital signs. Linear regression controlled for socioeconomic, maternal, nutritional, and healthcare factors. Compared to Naryn (n = 143), Bishkek children (n = 123) were taller (2.7 cm, p = 0.006), heavier (2.7 kg, p = 0.008), with larger waist (2.7 cm, p = 0.007) and mid-upper arm circumferences (0.7 cm, p = 0.023), lower hemoglobin (-14.4 g/L, p < 0.001), higher oxygen saturation (2.1%, p < 0.001), weaker hand-grip strength (-1.3 kgf, p = 0.013), and higher HAZ (0.5, p < 0.001). No differences existed in BMI or BAZ. Naryn males were shorter than females (-3.60 cm, p = 0.024). Bishkek children had lower FEV1 (-0.4, p = 0.006) and FVC z-scores (-0.48, p = 0.003). High-altitude Kyrgyz children showed developmental and respiratory patterns suggesting physiological adaptation, though malnutrition cannot be excluded. Lower birthweight partially explained reduced height but not lung function or male-specific growth, highlighting the need for altitude-specific growth and respiratory references and continued research in pediatric high-altitude populations.

items.title: Impact of Aerobic Exercise on Endothelial Function and Other Cardiovascular Disease Markers in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Meta-regression of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aerobic exercise (AE) has long been recognized as a potent stimulus for improving various cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related markers. Although several meta-analyses have focused on some of these markers, no meta-analysis or meta-regression has comprehensively evaluated the influence of multiple CVD-related markers on endothelial function, assessed by brachial-artery flow-mediated dilation (baFMD).
METHODS: This meta-analysis and meta-regression included randomized controlled trials investigating the effect of AE on baFMD. The primary outcome was pre- to post-intervention changes in baFMD. Secondary outcomes included endothelial blood biomarkers, hemodynamic measurements, cardiorespiratory fitness, body composition, glucose metabolism, and lipid profile. Pre- to post-intervention changes were summarized using a randomeffects model. Meta-regression analyses were performed to explore whether changes in secondary outcomes moderated changes in baFMD.
RESULTS: Seventy-two studies comprising 3357 participants were included. AE significantly improved baFMD (mean difference = 2.35%, p < 0.001), corresponding to an estimated 24% reduction in CVD risk. Significant improvements were observed across multiple CVD-related markers. Meta-regression revealed that changes in body weight and body fat (β = - 4.021 and - 1.721), systolic and diastolic blood pressure (β = - 0.525 and - 0.484), maximal oxygen uptake (β = 0.656), and insulin levels (β = 0.381) significantly moderated baFMD improvements.
CONCLUSIONS: AE elicits robust improvements in endothelial function and a wide range of CVD-related markers. This is the first meta-analysis to integrate these outcomes through meta-regression, demonstrating that exercise induced enhancements in body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, blood pressure and insulin regulation collectively contribute to endothelial adaptations. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the vascular benefits of AE and reinforce its role as a potent nonpharmacological strategy for CVD prevention and vascular health optimization. The protocol was prospectively registered in the Open Science Framework online registry (DOI: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/E4QYD ).

ai.titlePl: Wpływ treningu aerobowego na funkcję śródbłonka i markery chorób sercowo-naczyniowych: przegląd systematyczny i meta-analiza
ai.summary: Meta-analiza 72 randomizowanych badań (n=3357) wykazała, że trening aerobowy istotnie poprawia funkcję śródbłonka mierzoną przepływem przez tętnicę ramienną (baFMD o 2,35%, p<0,001), co odpowiada szacunkowej 24% redukcji ryzyka chorób sercowo-naczyniowych. Poprawa funkcji śródbłonka była pośredniczona przez zmniejszenie masy ciała i tłuszczu, obniżenie ciśnienia krwi, wzrost maksymalnego poboru tlenu oraz zmniejszenie poziomu insuliny.
ai.takeaway: Trener może z pewnością rekomendować trening aerobowy jako kluczowy element programu zdrowia sercowo-naczyniowego, ze szczególnym naciskiem na redukcję masy ciała, poprawę wydolności tlenowej i kontrolę metabolizmu glukozy.
ai.population: Różnorodna populacja badana (zdrowe osoby i pacjenci z chorobami), brak dokładnych danych demograficznych w abstrakcie
ai.limits: Duża heterogeniczność populacji (osoby zdrowe i chore); brak szczegółów dotyczących rodzaju, intensywności i czasu trwania treningów; wskaźnik funkeji śródbłonka (baFMD) jest wskaźnikiem pośrednim

items.title: Dose-dependent effects of sodium bicarbonate supplementation combined with sprint interval training on performance adaptations in basketball players: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sprint interval training (SIT) effectively improves physical performance in team-sport athletes, while sodium bicarbonate (Sb) supplementation may enhance training adaptations. However, the dose-dependent effects of Sb during SIT remain unclear in basketball players. Therefore, this study examined the effects of two Sb doses combined with SIT on physical performance adaptations in basketball players.
METHODS: Forty trained male basketball players (age: 21.6 ± 2.0 years, height: 185.4 ± 3.5 cm, body mass: 84.1 ± 4.4 kg) were recruited and randomly assigned to four groups: SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + placebo (PL) (n = 10), and control (CON) (n = 10). The intervention lasted four weeks during the preparatory phase of the season. Participants in the training groups performed SIT three times per week in addition to their regular basketball training. The SIT protocol consisted of four sets of ten 5-second maximal sprints, with 20 seconds of active recovery between repetitions and 2 minutes of rest between sets. All 40 enrolled participants successfully completed the 4-week intervention, resulting in a 0% dropout rate. Performance assessments conducted before and after the intervention included countermovement vertical jump (CMVJ), standing long jump (SLJ), 20 m sprint, Illinois change-of-direction speed (CODS), Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (Yo-Yo IR1), and Wingate anaerobic power (peak power output [PPO] and mean power output [MPO]).
RESULTS: All training groups showed significant improvements in physical performance variables over time (p < 0.05). Significant group by time interaction effects were observed for all performance variables (p ≤ 0.001), indicating that the SIT groups showed more gains compared with the CON group. Both Sb supplementation groups demonstrated greater improvements than the SIT + PL group in CMVJ, SLJ, sprint performance, CODS, Yo-Yo IR1 distance, PPO, and MPO (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb group exhibited significantly greater performance enhancements than the SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb group across all measured variables.
CONCLUSION: Four weeks of SIT improved performance in trained basketball players, with Sb supplementation providing additional dose-dependent benefits (0.45 > 0.3 g⋅kg-1). While the higher dose yielded superior adaptations, its practical application should be balanced against potential gastrointestinal discomfort and individual tolerance to ensure long-term athlete compliance.
items.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

ai.titlePl: Zależne od dawki efekty suplementacji wodorowęglanu sodu połączonej z treningiem sprintowym na adaptacje wydajnościowe u koszykarzy
ai.summary: Badanie na 40 wytrenowanych koszykarzach mężczyznach porównywało efekty 4-tygodniowego treningu sprintowego (SIT) w połączeniu z trzema wariantami suplementacji: wodorowęglanem sodu w dawce 0,3 g/kg, 0,45 g/kg lub placebo. Wszystkie grupy treningowe wykazały znaczną poprawę wydajności, jednak grupy stosujące wodorowęglan sodu uzyskały większe wzrosty we wszystkich testach (skok, sprint, zmiana kierunku, Yo-Yo test), a dawka 0,45 g/kg była istotnie bardziej efektywna niż 0,3 g/kg.
ai.takeaway: Trener może stosować wodorowęglan sodu w dawce 0,45 g/kgBody Mass podczas intensywnych treningów sprintowych u koszykarzy dla potencjalnie większych zysków wydajnościowych, jednak musi brać pod uwagę ryzyko dyskomfortu żołądkowo-jelitowego i tolerancję indywidualną.
ai.population: Wytrenowani koszykarze mężczyźni, 21,6±2,0 lat, n=40
ai.limits: Krótki okres interwencji (4 tygodnie), brak informacji o skutkach ubocznych i tolerancji żołądkowej, ograniczenie do populacji koszykarskiej

items.title: Motivational interviewing increases physical activity for adults with low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low back pain (LBP) is the leading cause of disability globally and contributes substantially to healthcare costs and lost productivity. Physical activity (PA) is recommended for managing LBP, nevertheless, many individuals with LBP remain insufficiently physically active, and strategies to support behavior change are needed. Motivational interviewing (MI) may support behavior change by enhancing intrinsic motivation and self-efficacy.
PURPOSE: To synthesize evidence on the effects of MI interventions targeting PA behavior in adults with LBP.
METHODS: Six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, CENTRAL, PsycINFO) and clinical trial registries were searched from inception to February 2026. Eligible trials evaluated MI-based interventions targeting PA in adults with acute, subacute, or chronic LBP. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD; Hedges' g) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). The primary outcome was change in PA; secondary outcomes included pain and disability-related outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Motivational interviewing-based interventions were associated with a statistically significant increase in PA compared with control conditions (SMD: 0.57; 95% CI, 0.10-1.03; P = .02), representing a moderate effect. No statistically significant effects were observed for pain (SMD: 0.04; 95% CI, -0.27 to 0.36; P = .76) or disability (SMD: 0.08; 95% CI, -0.25 to 0.40; P = .60). Certainty of evidence was low for PA and very low for pain and disability outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Motivational interviewing interventions were associated with increased PA in adults with LBP but did not demonstrate significant effects on pain or disability. MI may serve as a client-centered support strategy within broader rehabilitation models. Further high-quality trials with fidelity assessment and longer follow-up are warranted.
items.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine

ai.titlePl: Motywacyjny wywiad zwiększa aktywność fizyczną u dorosłych z bólem dolnego odcinka kręgosłupa: przegląd systematyczny i metaanaliza
ai.summary: Metaanaliza 6 baz danych oceniła wpływ interwencji motywacyjnego wywiadu (MI) na aktywność fizyczną u dorosłych z bólem dolnego odcinka kręgosłupa. MI było związane ze statystycznie istotnym wzrostem aktywności fizycznej (SMD: 0,57; 95% CI: 0,10–1,03; efekt umiarkowany), ale nie wykazało znaczących efektów na ból ani niepełnosprawność.
ai.takeaway: Trener może stosować elementy motywacyjnego wywiadu (fokus na wewnętrzną motywację, samoefektywność) w celu zwiększenia adherencji do aktywności fizycznej u klientów z bólem pleców, choć nie zmieni to bezpośrednio bólu czy funkcjonowania.
ai.population: Dorośli z ostrym, podostrzałym lub przewlekłym bólem dolnego odcinka kręgosłupa
ai.limits: Niska pewność dowodów, brak oceny wierności interwencji, krótki okres obserwacji, heterogenność protokołów MI

items.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and selected lipid outcomes in adult women with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and selected lipid outcomes in adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity.
METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261394616). PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and MEDLINE via Ovid were searched from database inception to 26 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials involving adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity and comparing HIIT with control conditions without structured exercise. Outcomes included body weight (BW), body mass index (BMI), body fat percentage (BF%), fat mass (FM), maximal or peak oxygen uptake (VO2max/VO2peak), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and triglycerides (TG). Hedges' g with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was used as the pooled effect measure, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Fifteen randomized controlled trials were included. Compared with controls without structured exercise, HIIT significantly reduced BW (g = -0.33, 95% CI -0.58 to -0.08; P = 0.01), BMI (g = -0.56, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.17; P< 0.01), BF% (g = -0.76, 95% CI -1.35 to -0.17; P = 0.01), and FM (g = -0.66, 95% CI -1.11 to -0.20; P< 0.01), and significantly improved VO2max/VO2peak (g = 1.09, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.47; P< 0.01). HIIT also increased HDL-C and reduced LDL-C, whereas effects on TC and TG were not statistically significant. Subgroup and meta-regression analyses were exploratory. Evidence certainty ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Current randomized evidence suggests that, compared with controls without structured exercise, HIIT may favor adiposity-related body-composition outcomes and cardiorespiratory fitness in adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity, whereas its effects on selected lipid outcomes remain uncertain. The review did not systematically evaluate other cardiometabolic outcomes, including blood pressure, insulin resistance, glycemic control, or inflammatory markers. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies, small sample sizes, between-study heterogeneity, and low to very low certainty of evidence.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261394616.

ai.titlePl: Wpływ treningu interwałowego wysokiej intensywności na kompozycję ciała, wydolność cardiorespiracyjną i lipidogram u dorosłych kobiet z nadwagą i otyłością
ai.summary: Przegląd systematyczny z metaanalizą 15 badań RCT porównujących HIIT z brakiem ćwiczeń u kobiet z nadwagą/otyłością. HIIT istotnie zmniejszył masę ciała (g=-0,33), BMI (g=-0,56), procent tkanki tłuszczowej (g=-0,76) i masę tłuszczową (g=-0,66) oraz poprawił VO2max/peak (g=1,09). Wpływ na cholesterol całkowity i triglicerydy nie był istotny statystycznie.
ai.takeaway: HIIT jest skutecznym narzędziem do redukcji masy ciała i poprawy wydolności u kobiet z nadwagą/otyłością; trener może włączyć HIIT do programu treningowego dla tego kontyngentu, choć efekty na profil lipidowy pozostają niepewne.
ai.population: Dorosłe kobiety z nadwagą, otyłością lub otyłością o normalnym BMI, n=nieznana (15 badań łącznie)
ai.limits: Niska do bardzo niskiej pewności dowodów, mała liczba badań, małe próby, heterogeniczność między badaniami

items.title: Neuromuscular, Balance, and Gait Factors Associated with Falls and Fall-Related Outcomes in Individuals with COPD: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have a higher incidence of falls than age-matched peers, which may result in injury, loss of independence, and reduced quality of life. Although falls have often been attributed to general deconditioning, impairments in muscle strength, balance, and gait may also contribute. This systematic review synthesized evidence on the relationships between these factors and falls or fall-related outcomes in people with COPD.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Knowledge, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched for English-language studies published up to November 2024. Twenty-five original studies involving 1295 participants met the inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified Downs and Black checklist.
RESULTS: Seventeen of the 25 studies reported a significant association between at least one examined factor and fall history or fall risk. Balance impairment showed the most consistent relationship, with positive associations reported in 14 of 17 studies. Evidence regarding muscle strength was mixed: some studies linked quadriceps weakness to increased fall risk, including one reporting an odds ratio of 2.9, whereas others found no significant association. Altered gait characteristics, particularly increased step-time variability, were also associated with falls.
CONCLUSION: Balance and gait impairments are consistently associated with falls and fall-related outcomes in individuals with COPD, whereas the relationship with muscle strength is less consistent. Given the predominance of observational studies, prospective research and controlled trials are needed to clarify causal pathways and determine whether targeted balance and strength training can reduce fall risk as part of pulmonary rehabilitation.
items.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
items.journalAbbr: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis

ai.titlePl: Czynniki neuromuskularne, równowagi i chodu związane z upadkami u osób z POChP: przegląd systematyczny
ai.summary: Przegląd 25 badań (n=1295) dotyczących związku między osłabieniem mięśni, równowagą i chodzeniem a upadkami u osób z POChP. Zaburzenia równowagi wykazały najsilniejszy związek z upadkami (14 z 17 badań), natomiast związek między siłą mięśni a upadkami był niejednorodny; zwiększona zmienność długości kroku wiązała się ze wzrostem ryzyka upadków.
ai.takeaway: Trener powinien priorytetowo uwzględnić treningi równowagi w pracy z klientami z POChP, natomiast sam trening siły może mieć mniejsze znaczenie; wymagane są badania kontrolne, by potwierdzić skuteczność interwencji.
ai.population: Osoby z POChP, mieszana płeć i wiek, łącznie n=1295 uczestników w 25 badaniach
ai.limits: Przewaga badań obserwacyjnych (nie eksperymentalnych), brak prospektywnych badań kontrolowanych potwierdzających przyczynowość

items.title: Reducing the risk of obesity, diabetes, and metabolic disorders in patients treated with antipsychotics - recommendations of the Polish Psychiatric Association Part I: risk factors and psychological interventions.
items.abstract: Patients suffering from mental disorders - particularly schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and depression - are at least 1.5 times more likely to develop metabolic disorders than the general population, with prevalence among people with mental disorders exceeding 30%. In 2019, the Polish Psychiatric Association (PTP) developed and published recommendations on reducing metabolic risk in patients with schizophrenia treated with antipsychotics (APs). This article presents the first part of the update and expansion of these recommendations. It focuses on risk factors for obesity, diabetes, and metabolic disorders in people treated with APs, as well as guidelines on non-pharmacological interventions to prevent and treat metabolic disorders. The recommendations were prepared by a group of experts invited by the Board of PTP based on a literature review, analysis of published guidelines, and clinical experience. Psychiatrists should not only be aware of the increased risk of metabolic disorders in people treated with APs but should also actively act to prevent these conditions. The basis of prevention is lifestyle modification through small, gradual steps easier to maintain over the long term. Recommended interventions include: (1) nutritional education, (2) regular physical activity, (3) meal planning, (4) menu preparation, (5) mindfulness and relaxation techniques, (6) participation in support groups, (7) progress monitoring. In cases of high risk, or when such disorders are already present, pharmacological interventions are recommended, as outlined in the second part of the guidelines.

ai.titlePl: Zmniejszanie ryzyka otyłości, cukrzycy i zaburzeń metabolicznych u pacjentów leczonych neuroleptycami – rekomendacje Polskiego Towarzystwa Psychiatrycznego
ai.summary: Pacjenci z zaburzeniami psychicznymi (szczególnie schizofrenią, zaburzeniem afektywnym dwubiegunowym, depresją) mają co najmniej 1,5 razy wyższe ryzyko zaburzeń metabolicznych niż populacja ogólna, z prevalencją przekraczającą 30%. Polskie Towarzystwo Psychiatryczne rekomenduje interwencje niefarmakologiczne: edukację żywieniową, regularną aktywność fizyczną, planowanie posiłków, techniki uważności i wsparcie grupowe.
ai.takeaway: Trener powinien być świadomy, że klienci przyjmujący neuroleptyki mają zwiększone ryzyko zaburzeń metabolicznych i mogą wymagać bardziej stopniowego podejścia do zmian stylu życia, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem małych, łatwych do utrzymania kroków.
ai.population: Pacjenci z zaburzeniami psychicznymi (schizofrenią, zaburzeniem afektywnym dwubiegunowym, depresją) leczeni neuroleptycami
ai.limits: Dokument stanowisku/wytyczne, a nie badanie randomizowane; skupia się na populacji psychiatrycznej, niekoniecznie na treningach siłowych

items.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training versus continuous aerobic training on body weight, body mass index, and body fat percentage in youth with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overweight and obesity in youth are associated with substantial short- and long-term health burdens, and structured exercise is a central component of management. Whether HIIT offers greater improvements in body composition than continuous aerobic training remains uncertain.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were searched from inception to December 31, 2024 for randomized trials directly comparing high-intensity interval-based training, including high-intensity interval exercise and sprint-interval protocols, with continuous aerobic training in youth with overweight or obesity. Outcomes were body weight, BMI, and body fat percentage. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2. Random-effects models with REML estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp inference generated mean differences (MDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity, subgroup, and small-study-effect analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Fourteen independent randomized trials were included. For body weight, 13 trials involving 409 participants showed no statistically significant difference between HIIT and continuous aerobic training (MD = -0.37 kg, 95% CI -0.89 to 0.15; P = 0.146; I 2 = 0%). For BMI, 14 trials involving 432 participants also showed no significant difference (MD = -0.14 kg/m2, 95% CI -0.31 to 0.02; P = 0.089; I 2 = 0%). For body fat percentage, 11 trials involving 331 participants showed no significant difference (MD = -0.33 percentage points, 95% CI -1.33 to 0.67; P = 0.481), with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 60.3%). Sensitivity analyses did not materially alter the findings, and subgroup analyses did not identify reliable effect modification by weekly frequency, intervention duration, or mean age. Egger's tests did not detect statistically significant small-study effects. One trial was at low overall risk of bias, whereas 13 raised some concerns.
CONCLUSION: Randomized evidence identified through December 31, 2024 does not show that HIIT provides greater reductions in body weight, BMI, or body fat percentage than continuous aerobic training. HIIT may be considered an alternative exercise format, but the limited evidence base and heterogeneity in body fat outcomes warrant cautious interpretation.

ai.titlePl: HIIT versus trening aerobowy w redukcji masy ciała u młodzieży z nadwagą i otyłością: przegląd systematyczny i metaanaliza
ai.summary: Metaanaliza 14 randomizowanych prób porównała wysokointensywny trening interwałowy (HIIT) z ciągłym treningiem aerobowym u 409–432 młodych osób z nadwagą lub otyłością. HIIT nie wykazał istotnie większej redukcji masy ciała (−0,37 kg), BMI (−0,14 kg/m²) ani procentu tkanki tłuszczowej (−0,33 p.p.) w porównaniu z treningiem aerobowym.
ai.takeaway: Trener może używać zarówno HIIT jak i trening aerobowy zamiennie w programach redukcji dla młodzieży z nadwagą, ponieważ efekty na skład ciała są porównywalne.
ai.population: Młodzież (średnia wieku nie sprecyzowana w abstrakcie) z nadwagą lub otyłością, n=331–432 w poszczególnych analizach
ai.limits: Tylko 1 z 14 badań miało niskie ryzyko błędu; znaczna heterogenność wyników dla procentu tkanki tłuszczowej (I²=60,3%); ograniczona baza dowodów

items.title: Effects of time-restricted eating on body composition and performance in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Time-restricted eating (TRE) has gained increasing attention as a dietary strategy for body mass management and metabolic health. However, its efficacy in athletic populations remains unclear. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine the effects of TRE on energy intake, body composition, and performance in athletes.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, the review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261291351). Six databases were searched from inception to January 10, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing TRE with non-TRE dietary patterns in adult athletes were included if they reported body composition or performance outcomes. Pooled effects were estimated as standardized mean differences (SMDs; Hedges' g) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and evidence certainty using GRADE.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies from 15 articles involving 245 athletes were included. TRE did not significantly alter energy intake (SMDpooled = -0.35, 95%CI: -0.77 to 0.07, p = 0.11). Compared with non-TRE dietary patterns, TRE resulted in small but significant reductions in body mass (SMDpooled = -0.27, 95%CI: -0.50 to -0.04; p = 0.02) and body fat% (SMDpooled = -0.39, 95%CI: -0.68 to -0.11, p = 0.01), while fat mass (SMDpooled = -0.23, 95%CI: -0.48 to 0.02, p = 0.07) and lean mass (SMDpooled = -0.16, 95%CI: -0.42 to 0.09, p = 0.21) were unchanged. TRE had no significant effects on aerobic capacity (SMDpooled = 0.04, 95%CI: -0.29 to 0.37, p = 0.82), muscular endurance (SMDpooled = -0.20, 95%CI: -0.52 to 0.13, p = 0.23), muscular strength (SMDpooled = 0.01, 95%CI: -0.25 to 0.27, p = 0.94), or power (SMDpooled = -0.12, 95%CI: -0.44 to 0.20, p = 0.47). Subgroup analyses suggested potentially greater reductions in body mass and body fat% among elite athletes, although between-subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.
CONCLUSION: TRE may represent a feasible dietary strategy for athletes seeking modest reductions in body mass and body fat% without clear detrimental effects on performance. However, evidence remains limited by small samples, short interventions, and methodological concerns, warranting larger, well-controlled, and longer-term trials across diverse athletic populations.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO unique identifier CRD420261291351.

ai.titlePl: Wpływ jedzenia w ograniczonym czasowo na skład ciała i wydajność sportową: przegląd systematyczny i metaanaliza
ai.summary: Przegląd obejmujący 16 badań z 245 sportowcami porównywał jedzenie w ograniczonym przedziale czasowym (TRE) z innymi sposobami odżywiania. TRE spowodowało małe, ale istotne zmniejszenie masy ciała (SMD: -0,27) i procentu tkanki tłuszczowej (SMD: -0,39), bez wpływu na wydajność (siłę, wytrzymałość, pojemność aerową).
ai.takeaway: TRE może być wdrożone jako opcja dla klientów chcących skromnego obniżenia masy i tkanki tłuszczowej, ale nie jest konieczne do budowy siły lub hipertrofii mięśniowej.
ai.population: Dorosłi sportowcy (elitarni i amatorzy), n=245 w 16 badaniach
ai.limits: Małe próby, krótkie interwencje, niejednorodna jakość badań, bardzo niska do umiarkowanej pewność dowodów

items.title: Effects of Tabata-style functional training and cinnamon supplementation on army combat fitness test performance, serum irisin, and body composition in military cadets: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract:
AIM: The study aimed to assess the effect of Tabata-style functional training with or without cinnamon supplementation on the performance of the Army Combat Fitness Test (ACFT), serum irisin levels, and body composition in cadets at military academies.
METHODS: In a randomized controlled design, 48 male cadets (22.8 ± 1.3 years) were allocated to 4 groups: Tabata group (n = 14), cinnamon group (n = 10), Tabata+cinnamon (n = 14), and control group (n = 10). This was a 6-week intervention. Tabata training was performed three times per week (8 × 20s work/10s rest; 87%-95% HRmax), and cinnamon (Cinnamomum zeylanicum) supplementation was administered three times per day (1.5g per day). The ACFT components, serum irisin, body fat percentage (BFP), visceral fat index (VFI), lean body mass (LBM), and body mass index (BMI) were evaluated before and after treatment.
RESULTS: The group × time interaction was significant for ACFT score, irisin, and body composition markers (p < 0.001). Bonferroni post hoc showed that ACFT test scores in both groups, COMB and TAB, improved significantly compared to the CON group (p < 0.05). Significant improvement was observed for groups COMB and TAB in 3 repetition maximum Deadlift, Standing Power Throw, Release Pushups, Sprint-Drag-Carry, Leg Tuck, and 2-Mile Run compared to CON group (p < 0.05). The most significant increase in serum irisin levels was observed in COMB group compared to the other groups (p < 0.001). All groups showed significant reductions in body weight, BMI, and VFI when compared to the control group (p < 0.05). Among the groups, TAB group had a remarkably lower BFP than the others (p < 0.001). Additionally, LBM increased significantly in all groups compared to the control group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Tabata-style training combined with cinnamon supplementation markedly enhanced performance, body composition, and circulating irisin in young male military cadets, yielding significant improvements in functional capacity and demonstrating the advantage of pairing high-intensity exercise with targeted nutritional intervention.
items.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

ai.titlePl: Trening Tabata ze świetlnością kardio a suplementacja cynamonem: wpływ na test zdolności bojowej, irisynę i skład ciała u kadetów wojskowych
ai.summary: Badanie obejmowało 48 młodych mężczyzn (22,8 ± 1,3 lat) podzielonych na 4 grupy: Tabata, cynamonida, kombinacja i kontrola. Po 6 tygodniach treningu Tabata (3x/tydz., 87-95% HRmax) połączonego z cynamonem (1,5 g/dzień) wykazano istotną poprawę wyniku w Army Combat Fitness Test (p < 0,05) oraz wzrost irisyny w stosunku do grupy kontrolnej. Grupy treningowe zmniejszyły procent tkanki tłuszczowej, BMI i wskaźnik tłuszczu trzewnego, a zvększyły mięśniową masę ciała (p < 0,05).
ai.takeaway: Trener może wdrożyć 6-tygodniowy cykl treningu Tabata (3x/tydzień, 87-95% HRmax) połączony ze zwiększonym spożyciem cynamonu dla szybkiej poprawy wydolności funkcjonalnej i składu ciała u sportowców wysokowydajnych.
ai.population: Wytrenowani mężczyźni kadeci wojskowi, wiek ~23 lata, n=48
ai.limits: Krótkiczas badania (6 tygodni), małej próba, populacja specjalistyczna (kadeci wojskowi), brak danych o trwałości efektów; rola cynamonu w izolacji słabo zdefiniowana

items.title: Apathy and Physical Activity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Purpose: Patient motivation is essential for successful rehabilitation, so apathy may hinder physiotherapists' interventions aimed at increasing physical activity. We examined the relationship between apathy and physical activity to identify the factors that influence it. Methods: Pearson product-moment correlations were pooled from eligible studies to examine the relationship between apathy and physical activity. Subgroup meta-analyses and meta-regressions were also conducted. Results: From the systematic review (28 articles) and main meta-analysis (22 studies; N = 12,541), the results showed a negative correlation between apathy and physical activity (r = -0.13; 95% CI: -0.18, -0.09; p < 0.0001 based on Pearson's r-values; r = -0.40; 95% CI: -0.68, -0.02; p = 0.043 based on Spearman's ρ-values). The correlation was statistically significant in patients with Parkinson's disease and in older adults who were healthy, depressed, fallers, or had mild cognitive impairment. A meta-regression showed an effect of age, with a stronger correlation between apathy and physical activity in older adults compared to younger adults (p = 0.003). Conclusion: Higher levels of apathy are associated with lower levels of physical activity, and this negative association is stronger with age. Therefore, apathy may limit exercise therapy efficacy and carry prognostic implications for patients whose condition requires physical activity.

ai.titlePl: Apatia i aktywność fizyczna: przegląd systematyczny i meta-analiza
ai.summary: Przegląd 28 artykułów (meta-analiza 22 badań, n=12 541) wykazał istotną ujemną korelację między apią a aktywnością fizyczną (r=-0,13, p<0,0001). Związek był szczególnie silny u pacjentów z chorobą Parkinsona i u starszych dorosłych. Korelacja wzmacniała się z wiekiem (p=0,003).
ai.takeaway: Trener powinien rozpoznać i pracować nad zwiększeniem motywacji pacjentów (szczególnie starszych), ponieważ apatia znacząco obniża zgodność z treningiem i efektywność interwencji.
ai.population: Pacjenci z różnymi stanami klinicznymi (choroba Parkinsona, starsi dorośli zdrowi i z chorobami) oraz ogółem starsze osoby dorosłe, n=12 541
ai.limits: Heterogeniczna populacja i warianty definicji apatii; słaba korelacja (r=-0,13) może mieć ograniczoną znaczenie kliniczne

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for obstructive sleep apnea: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: Weight reduction is recommended in all overweight and obese patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists-based therapies have demonstrated clinical benefits in reducing weight and could potentially improve OSA outcomes. We aim to analyze the efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists-based therapies in patients with moderate-to-severe OSA.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared GLP-1 receptor agonists-based therapies versus control in adults with moderate-to-severe OSA. We systematically searched electronic databases and registries up to February 10, 2025. Outcomes assessed included apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), body weight, oxygen desaturation index (ODI), minimum oxygen saturation, systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 6 RCTs involving 1,069 participants were included, four evaluating liraglutide and two tirzepatide. Compared with control, GLP-1 receptor agonist-based therapies reduced AHI by - 9.99 events/hour (95% CI, - 16.47 to - 3.50; p < 0.01; I2 = 87%) and body weight by - 9.68 kg (95% CI, - 15.84 to - 3.51; p < 0.01; I2 = 98%). These therapies also reduced SBP by -4.77 mmHg (95% CI, -7.04 to -2.51; p < 0.01), and DBP by -1.41 mmHg (95% CI, -2.71 to -0.11; p = 0.03). No significant differences were observed in ODI or minimum oxygen saturation. GLP-1 receptor agonists-based therapies did not increase the risk of adverse events.
CONCLUSION: GLP-1 receptor agonist-based therapies reduced AHI and body weight in the populations studied. Substantial heterogeneity limits interpretation of the pooled effect magnitude. These findings support their potential role within comprehensive OSA management but do not establish them as substitutes for CPAP.
REGISTRY: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; No.: CRD42024564018; URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ .

ai.titlePl: Agonisty receptora GLP-1 w leczeniu obturacyjnego bezdechu sennego: metaanaliza badań randomizowanych
ai.summary: Metaanaliza 6 badań randomizowanych (n=1069) porównała agonisty GLP-1 z placebo u pacjentów z umiarkowanym do ciężkim obturacyjnym bezdechu sennym. Terapia zmniejszyła indeks apnoe-hipopnoe o 9,99 zdarzeń/godzinę, wagę ciała o 9,68 kg oraz ciśnienie skurczowe o 4,77 mmHg.
ai.takeaway: Agonisty GLP-1 mogą wspierać redukcję wagi i poprawę wskaźników OSA u otyłych klientów, ale nie zastępują CPAP i stanowią dodatek do kompleksowego leczenia.
ai.population: Dorośli z umiarkowanym do ciężkim obturacyjnym bezdechu sennym, n=1069 (głównie badania z liraglutydą i tirzepatydą)
ai.limits: Duża niejednorodność wyników (I²=87-98%), brak badań długoterminowych, populacja z OSA (pacjenci medyczni, nie typowi klienci siłowni)

items.title: Acute caffeine intervention and cognitive performance in populations aged 20 years and younger: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the acute effects of caffeine supplementation on cognitive performance in healthy populations aged 20 years and younger, and to explore potential moderators including dose, cognitive domain, population type, and outcome measure.
METHODS: Four databases (Web of Science, PubMed, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library) were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials and randomized crossover trials assessing the effects of acute oral caffeine versus placebo on cognitive outcomes in individuals aged ≤20 years were included. A two-level meta-analytic model was used to calculate pooled standardized mean differences (SMD). Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were performed to explore potential methodological moderators influencing the overall effect.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies comprising 250 participants and 37 effect sizes were included. Caffeine demonstrated a small positive effect on cognitive task performance compared with placebo (SMD = 0.41, 95% CI 0.28-0.55; p < 0.01), with low heterogeneity (I2 = 10%). Meta-regression showed no significant moderating influences of age, acute supplementation dose, habitual daily intake, and acute-to-habitual dose ratio on caffeine-induced cognitive improvements. However, limited statistical power may restrict the interpretability of this result. Subgroup analyses showed that cognitive domain, outcome measure type, participant population, administration route, and sex did not significantly moderate caffeine's cognitive effects. Notably, however, when comparing outcome measure types, the enhancement magnitude of caffeine on reaction time was greater than that on accuracy, with this difference approaching statistical significance (p = 0.08). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings, and no publication bias was detected.
CONCLUSION: Among individuals aged 20 and younger, acute caffeine ingestion produces a small yet statistically significant beneficial effect on cognitive performance. Specifically, moderate improvements were observed in psychomotor speed and attention, alongside smaller gains in executive function. No significant moderators influencing this ergogenic effect were identified in the present meta-analysis. Importantly, the conclusion that habitual caffeine intake exerts no moderating impact is derived from only seven studies and may be limited by insufficient statistical power. These findings offer tentative support for the judicious use of caffeine to boost cognition among young athletes and healthy adolescents, yet caution is warranted given the small number of small-sample studies.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: This systematic review has been registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews) under registration number CRD420261342996.

ai.titlePl: Wpływ kafeiny na wydolność poznawczą u osób poniżej 20 lat: przegląd systematyczny i meta-analiza
ai.summary: Przegląd 14 badań (n=250, 37 wielkości efektów) dotyczących wpływu akutnego spożycia kafeiny na funkcje poznawcze u osób ≤20 lat. Kofeinę porównano z placebo i wykazano mały pozytywny efekt (SMD=0,41, 95% CI 0,28–0,55; p<0,01) z niską heterogenością. Największe poprawy w szybkości psychomotorycznej i uwadze, mniejsze w funkcjach wykonawczych.
ai.takeaway: U młodych sportowców i adolescentów kofeinę można rozważać jako ergogenną do poprawy uwagi i szybkości reakcji, ale wyniki dotyczą populacji zdrowotnej, a liczba badań jest mała.
ai.population: Osoby zdolne (młode, ≤20 lat), głównie sportowcy i zdrowi nastoletni; n=250
ai.limits: Mała liczba badań źródłowych (n=14), małe próby uczestników w poszczególnych pracach, niewystarczająca moc statystyczna do oceny moderatorów (zwłaszcza wpływu habituacyjnego spożycia kafeiny na tylko 7 badaniach)

items.title: Designing helpful food labels: a randomized trial comparing effects of Physical Activity Calorie Equivalent and Health Star Rating labels on product perception and choice.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Front-of-pack labelling could help consumers choose healthier options over energy-dense, nutrient-poor alternatives.
PURPOSE: We assessed the effects of Health Star Rating (HSRs) and Physical Activity Calorie Equivalent (PACE) labels on adults' food and beverage choices and explored possible mechanisms by which these 2 labelling systems may have their effects.
METHODS: In an online experiment, 1268 Australian adults (18-59 years) were randomized to: no labels (control), PACE, or HSR labels. Participants were shown snack and drink options with varying energy content and nutritional profiles. Participants rated the healthiness and energy content of each product, completed a choice task, and rated both labelling systems in relation to their effects on motivation, emotional responses and perceived label credibility.
RESULTS: Compared to no labels, both HSR and PACE labels increased identification of unhealthy products, while only HSRs increased identification of healthy products. PACE labels prompted more accurate perceptions of energy content for high- and low-energy products compared to HSR labels and no labels. Both PACE and HSR labels prompted a greater proportion of healthy choices, but only PACE labels prompted a greater proportion of "optimal" that is, low-energy and healthy choices. Participants in the PACE condition were more motivated to reduce daily energy intake and take more exercise. Label-induced motivation mediated the effects of labels on optimal product choice.
CONCLUSIONS: PACE labels were most effective in prompting accurate perceptions of the energy content of products and in facilitating optimal (healthy and low-energy) choices. Mediation analyses suggested that this may be due to greater behavior-change motivation generated by PACE labels.
items.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine

ai.titlePl: Porównanie etykiet PACE i Health Star Rating: wpływ na percepcję produktów i wybory żywieniowe dorosłych
ai.summary: W badaniu randomizowanym 1268 australijskich dorosłych (18–59 lat) porównano wpływ braku etykiet, etykiet PACE (fizyczna aktywność równoważna kalorii) i HSR (oceny zdrowotne) na wybory żywieniowe i percepcję produktów. Etykiety PACE były najskuteczniejsze w poprawie dokładnej percepcji zawartości energetycznej i wyborze optymalnych produktów (niskoenergentycznych i zdowych), zwiększając również motywację do redukcji kalorycznej i aktywności fizycznej.
ai.takeaway: Trener może rekomendować klientom produkty z etykietami PACE zamiast tradycyjnych, ponieważ zwiększają one świadomość zawartości energetycznej i motywację do zmian behawioralnych.
ai.population: Dorośli australijscy 18–59 lat, n=1268, populacja ogólna (online)
ai.limits: Badanie online w warunkach laboratoryjnych, a nie rzeczywiste wybory w sklepie; populacja australijska; brak danych na temat długoterminowych efektów

items.title: Acute effects of 3 and 6 mg·Kg-1 caffeine on strength-power performance and isokinetic peak torque in competitive male boxers: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the dose, timing, and task specificity of caffeine ingestion in combat-sport athletes remains limited. This study examined the acute effects of 3 and 6 mg·kg-1 caffeine on strength-power performance and isokinetic peak torque in male boxers.
METHODS: Fifteen male boxers who met the Chinese national second-class athlete standard or higher completed a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Each participant completed placebo (PLA), 3 mg·kg-1 caffeine (CAF3), and 6 mg·kg-1 caffeine (CAF6) conditions in randomized order, separated by a 1-week washout. Countermovement jump (CMJ), ballistic push-up (BPU), and dominant-side shoulder and knee isokinetic peak torque (PT) were assessed at baseline and during testing blocks beginning at 30 and 60 min post-ingestion. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, with Holm adjustment applied across the 10 planned condition × time interaction tests. Reliability analyzes were supportive, and threshold-based individual classifications were exploratory.
RESULTS: Significant condition × time interactions were observed for CMJ, BPU, and isokinetic PT outcomes. During the scheduled 60-min assessment, CAF3 and CAF6 produced higher CMJ jump height, peak power, and relative peak power than PLA, with no significant difference between caffeine doses. For BPU, CAF6 produced higher concentric impulse, concentric mean power, and concentric peak power than PLA during the scheduled 60-min assessment, whereas CAF3 did not differ from PLA. Shoulder flexion and extension PT increased under caffeine conditions at selected time points, without a consistent dose advantage. Knee extension PT showed the clearest dose-specific response, with CAF6 exceeding both PLA and CAF3 during the scheduled 60-min assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute ingestion of 3 and 6 mg·kg-1 caffeine was associated with improvements in selected laboratory-based strength-power and isokinetic PT outcomes in male boxers, particularly during the scheduled 60-min assessment. The pattern of responses varied across doses and testing tasks, and 6 mg·kg-1 was not consistently superior to 3 mg·kg-1. These findings should be interpreted as evidence for selected neuromuscular outcomes rather than as direct evidence of improved punching or competitive boxing performance.
items.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

ai.titlePl: Wpływ kawy 3 i 6 mg/kg na siłę, moc i moment obrotowy u bokserów – badanie kontrolowane placebo
ai.summary: 15 bokserów zawodowych porównano w badaniu krzyżowym, otrzymując placebo lub kofeinę w dawce 3 lub 6 mg/kg. Po 60 minutach obie dawki kawy zwiększyły wysokość skoku CMJ i moc szczytową, a 6 mg/kg poprawiło moc eksplozywną w pompkach balistycznych i moment kolanowy bardziej niż 3 mg/kg.
ai.takeaway: Trener może stosować kofeinę 3–6 mg/kg u bokserów ok. 60 minut przed treningiem siłowo-moc, ale wynik dotyczy testów laboratoryjnych, nie potwierdza bezpośrednio poprawy wydajności boksowania.
ai.population: Bokserzy zawodowi (mężczyźni), spełniający standard drugiej klasy atlety krajowego, n=15
ai.limits: Próba bardzo mała (n=15), wyniki dotyczą testów izometrycznych i skoków, nie rzeczywistej wydajności boksowania; brak bezpośredniego pomiaru siły punchu

items.title: Effect of tangeretin supplements on simulated precompetition weight loss in female combat sports athletes.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight reduction before competition has long been a major challenge for combat-sports athletes. Unscientific weight-loss practices not only increase the risk of hormonal imbalance, electrolyte disturbance, and impaired immune function but also compromise athletic capacities such as aerobic and anaerobic performance and explosive power. This study investigated the potential benefits of tangeretin, a natural citrus extract, on athletic performance. These benefits include the regulation of hormone secretion, the optimization of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, and the promotion of muscle synthesis and lipid utilization, which may help athletes reach their target weight.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the effects of tangeretin supplementation on body-composition and sports-performance indicators in female combat-sports athletes, and to evaluate its efficacy for simulated precompetition weight loss.
METHODS: Thirty female combat-sports athletes (4 wrestlers, 3 boxers, 9 sanda athletes, 3 judokas, and 11 taekwondo athletes) were recruited. A paired, randomized, double-blind design was used. All 30 participants were first paired according to sport and competitive level, then randomly allocated to either a tangeretin group or a placebo group (15 per group). The 30-day intervention comprised a double-blind nutritional supplement, a dietary questionnaire, blood sampling and analysis, body-composition assessment, isokinetic muscle-strength testing, and aerobic-capacity testing, to evaluate the effects of tangeretin (400 mg/day) on performance and health-related outcomes. These outcomes included body-composition indicators (e.g. body-fat percentage, fat mass, lean-body mass), fat-distribution indicators (e.g. limb and regional fat mass, gynoid fat mass), glucose and lipid-metabolism indicators (e.g. LDL-C, total cholesterol, free fatty acids), hormone indicators (e.g. cortisol, testosterone), muscle-strength indicators (e.g. peak torque of hip, knee, and ankle flexors and extensors), and maximal-oxygen-uptake-derived indicators (e.g. VO2max heart rate, time to exhaustion). Statistical significance was assessed using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).
RESULTS: (1) Body weight: 80.0% of athletes in the tangeretin group lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% (5 athletes) reached their competition weight class. (2) Body fat: body-fat percentage in the tangeretin group decreased from 23.92 ± 0.87% to 22.92 ± 0.89%; trunk, upper-limb, lower-limb, and android-region fat mass decreased by 6.77%, 8.77%, 4.43%, and 8.09%, respectively. (3) Glucose and lipid metabolism: HDL-C increased by 8.86% (P = 0.002), whereas triglycerides decreased by 25.00% (P = 0.048). (4) Sports performance: peak torque during hip, knee, and ankle flexion and extension increased significantly in the tangeretin group. VO2max also improved from 42.80 ± 1.13 to 43.46 ± 1.32 ml/kg/min.
CONCLUSION: Tangeretin supplementation effectively reduced body weight and fat mass (both overall and regionally) in female combat-sports athletes. Among the participants, 80.0% lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% reached their competition weight class, indicating a strong effect on precompetition weight loss. Moreover, tangeretin improved aerobic capacity and lower-limb joint muscle strength, thereby enhancing competitive performance.
items.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

ai.titlePl: Wpływ suplementacji tangeretyny na redukcję wagi przed konkurencją u zawodniczek sportów walki
ai.summary: Badanie na 30 zawodniczkach sportów walki (zapaśniczki, bokserki, judoczki, zawodniczki taekwondo) porównywało suplementację tangeretyny (400 mg/dzień) z placebo przez 30 dni. Grupa tangeretyny osiągnęła zmniejszenie tkanki tłuszczowej o ~1% masy ciała (23,92% → 22,92%), 80% uczestniczek straciło wagę, a 33,3% osiągnęło docelową wagę konkurencyjną; ponadto VO2max wzrosło z 42,80 do 43,46 ml/kg/min i uległa poprawie siła mięśni dolnych kończyn.
ai.takeaway: Tangeretyna może wspomóc redukcję wagi i poprawę wydolności w przygotowaniu do konkurencji u zawodniczek sportów walki, jednak dla typowych klientów siłowni wynik ma ograniczone zastosowanie ze względu na specjalność populacji.
ai.population: Zawodniczki sportów walki (zapaśniczki, bokserki, judoczki, taekwondo, sanda), n=30, średnia waga ~80 kg
ai.limits: Bardzo mała i specjalistyczna populacja (tylko kobiety, sportowcy walki), krótki okres 30 dni, brak informacji o dawkowaniu tangeretyny w praktyce

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of non-surgical interventions and their combinations for the prevention of breast cancer-related lymphedema: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aims of this study were to compare the relative effectiveness of non-surgical preventive interventions and their combinations on breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL) incidence and shoulder abduction range of motion (ROM) using Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) and to assess the certainty of evidence using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework.
METHODS: Eight databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed) were searched through January 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of non-surgical interventions for BCRL prevention in post-surgical breast cancer patients were included. The primary outcome was BCRL incidence, which was analyzed using a Bayesian random-effects NMA with arm-level binomial likelihood and log link (risk ratio). The primary analysis was restricted to studies with a follow-up of at least 6 months, based on evidence that the risk of BCRL in axillary lymph node dissection populations peaks at 6-12 months postoperatively. A meta-regression with follow-up duration as a covariate was conducted on the full 45-study network to validate this restriction. Shoulder abduction ROM was analyzed as a secondary outcome after data cleaning to ensure measurement homogeneity.
RESULTS: A total of 100 RCTs were included in the qualitative synthesis. The primary BCRL analysis comprised 27 studies (57 arms, 4,660 participants, 11 nodes). Seven interventions showed credible intervals excluding 1: compression therapy combined with resistance training (COMP+RT) [risk ratio (RR) = 0.146, 95% credible interval (95%CrI) = 0.057-0.366, surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) = 85.1%], RT with supervised exercise (RT+SUP-EX) (RR = 0.147, 95%CrI = 0.019-0.665, SUCRA = 80.8%), COMP with manual lymphatic drainage (COMP+MLD) (RR = 0.121, 95%CrI = 0.004-0.915, SUCRA = 80.6%), intermittent pneumatic compression with MLD (IPC+MLD) (RR = 0.255, 95%CrI = 0.153-0.397, SUCRA = 69.3%), microwave therapy (MW) (RR = 0.313, 95%CrI = 0.090-0.926, SUCRA = 57.8%), IPC (RR = 0.396, 95%CrI = 0.197-0.765, SUCRA = 47.8%), and MLD (RR = 0.467, 95%CrI = 0.320-0.650, SUCRA = 39.2%). COMP+RT ranked first in three of six analytical approaches. However, it was excluded as a sparse node under stricter diagnostic definitions. The meta-regression coefficient for follow-up duration was statistically significant (β = 0.077/month, 95%CrI = 0.026-0.128), confirming that the treatment effects attenuated with longer follow-up. The cleaned ROM analysis (12 studies, 1,079 participants, 11 nodes) identified eight interventions with credible intervals excluding zero, led by acupoint massage with isokinetic strength training (AM+ISO) [mean difference (MD) = 22.83°, 95%CrI = 11.06-34.89, SUCRA = 85.2%]. Two interventions ranked in the top four for both outcomes: COMP+RT (BCRL rank 1 and ROM rank 4) and IPC+MLD (BCRL rank 4 and ROM rank 3).
CONCLUSION: COMP+RT demonstrated the most robust evidence profile among all evaluated interventions, ranking first for BCRL incidence in three of six analytical approaches and in the top four for shoulder ROM.
